sourceFacts.reviewScope: Complete static medium-fi tower exterior. Original detailed heritage recipe remains byte-reproducible. Published 16.5 m cylinder, 31 m north-side height envelope, smooth lower 12 m, upper raised masonry courses, western arched doorway, eight narrow slit indications, circular open roof parapet and asymmetric rounded seaside buttress remain. The reviewed roof restores an inset buttress terrace and closed parapet instead of the draft solid top slab; a small sloping stairhead is proportionally interpreted from the reserve illustration and satellite roof context, not a measured current fitting. Forty-three course positions and slit heights are photographic estimates, not a block survey. Skyline/district average course groups into broad low-contrast tonal zones; street/closeup preserve individual physical raised bands. The original inscription panel preserves published dimensions without invented text. Museum interior, well, buried foundations and separately mapped adjoining low defensive buildings are separate scope. No private bitmap is embedded; two canonical shared material graphs supply metric limestone and painted metal. Ground0 is the lowest exterior base, not the roof, and the reported three-metre grade difference requires real terrain fitting. Flat fixtures cannot certify slope or foundation contact. Cached exact-QID OSM outline and actual north-up satellite establish the directed eastern/southeastern arm; projected roof displacement prevents surveyed placement. Native footprint is retained and replacement disabled.

appearance.identity: Baku limestone tower with its asymmetric seaside buttress, rounded nose, relief masonry bands, recessed slit openings and open roof parapet.
appearance.master: Complete reviewed exterior; original detailed source preserved.
appearance.browser: Whole cylinder, asymmetric rounded buttress, recessed western doorway, roof parapets and slit indications at all four levels; near levels retain individual physical raised courses.

geographic.evidence: Cached attributed OSM way299418016 for Q842822, captured2026-09-27T16:21:24.079Z, supplies the17-point asymmetric outline and center[49.837270733,40.366150763]. Actual north-up Google satellite inspected2026-10-09 confirms the cylinder west of the rounded eastern/southeastern arm beside Neftchilar Avenue. Heading0.081716996579rad maps native+X slightly north of east and the western doorway toward west/slightly south. Published Presidential Library text independently identifies the western arched entrance. Roof/shadow displacement and map generalization leave approximately two-metre positional and five-degree angular uncertainty. The rebuilt fixture checks this signed transform, not a surveyed roof or terrain fit.
